The print is drawn from its own G-code: the outside walls of every layer, in the colour loaded in the head that prints them. While it prints, the nozzle runs along that G-code and is checked against the printer's own position about four times a second, so the walls appear where and when they are laid. The chamber light, the fans, the filament moving in its tube, the spools and the belts follow the printer's own readings. The printer reports no feeder speed, so a load or an unload is drawn as a push or pull of a typical size when a filament sensor changes or you press Feed. The belt teeth are larger than real ones and run as far as the head does.
